title: Clergy, laity, religious (CCC 871–945)
hookLine: different callings in one people, equal in dignity

lines: A PANTRY, A STUDY, AN OFFICE.
cards: Tuesday morning at a parish. A retired nurse unlocks the food pantry and starts sorting cans. Down the hall, a sister in a plain habit runs a Bible study for new mothers.
The pastor is in the office, on the phone with a family planning a funeral. A teenager is setting up chairs for confirmation class.

A man who'll never set foot in the office is, at that moment, telling the truth at work when it would be easier not to. Which of them is the Church? The Catechism's answer is all of them, in different callings.

teach.b: The Catechism begins with what everyone shares. All the baptized share in Christ's work as priest, prophet and king, each in their own way.
Then a strong line: among all the faithful there is a true equality of dignity and of action, because all are reborn in Christ.
Paul says it about gifts, in the Douay-Rheims: "there are diversities of ministries, but the same Lord." Different jobs, same Lord, same dignity. Then the callings.
Clergy are those ordained, as bishops, priests and deacons, to teach, sanctify and lead in Christ's name.
Religious take vows of poverty, chastity and obedience in a community the Church recognizes: the sister running the Bible study.
And the laity are everyone else among the faithful: all except those in holy orders and those in the religious state.
A definition by what they aren't, but it doesn't stop there.
The laity have their own calling, a secular one: they seek God's kingdom by engaging in ordinary affairs, family, work, politics, culture, and ordering them toward God.
The nurse sorting cans and the man telling the truth at work aren't helping the Church from outside; the Catechism says some people will hear the gospel only through them.
Acts has an early picture: Priscilla and Aquila, a married couple who made tents, take a gifted preacher named Apollos aside and explain the way of God to him more fully.
The Catechism also quotes Pope Pius the Twelfth saying of lay believers that they are the Church. Different callings, no ranks of worth.

teach.h: DIVERSITIES OF MINISTRIES, BUT THE SAME LORD.
teach.b: A bishop, a sister and a bus driver stand before God with the same baptism.

how: In Catholic parishes lay people serve as readers, catechists, musicians and parish council members, and Catholic teaching sees their everyday work and family life as their particular share in the Church's mission.

o: people who've left the Church but stay baptized
church volunteers with official parish jobs
all the faithful who aren't ordained or vowed

games.q: clergy, laity, religious — tap the pairs.
p: the faithful not ordained or vowed

s: the Catechism ranks clergy above laity in dignity
it says there is a true equality of dignity among all the faithful.
the laity's calling is mainly in the world: family, work, public life
the Catechism calls it their secular calling.
the Catechism quotes a pope saying lay believers are the Church
Pius the Twelfth: they are the Church.

games.q: you're Priscilla and Aquila, a married couple who make tents. a gifted preacher named Apollos is teaching boldly, but he knows only the baptism of John. what do you do?
o: correct him in front of everyone
take him aside and explain the way of God more fully
games.why: Acts says they took him to them and expounded the way of the Lord to him more carefully. tentmakers, teaching a preacher.

practice: Bring to mind someone who gives their time to a church or a community without a collar or a title, the person who runs the food drive, teaches the class, plays the piano, visits the sick, keeps the books, and think of one specific thing they did that helped.
If you pray, thank God for them by name; if you don't, just let the thanks sit in you.

wordCard.voice: Laity. All the faithful not ordained or in religious life, bringing the kingdom into daily life. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: equal dignity. Tuesday at the parish, every one of them the Church. I'll be here tomorrow.
